prize_parts.citation: for developing targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins

statement.case_for: I keep targeted protein degradation as a single prize part with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. After round 1 the case rests on more than headcount: four members independently arrived at the same trio or a near relative of it, and the chair's summary shows the objections are attribution and clinical timing, not whether the chemistry works. The mechanism is the kind I look for, a simple idea (a small molecule that forces proximity between a target and an E3 ligase) that was demonstrated in vitro, in cells and structurally, and has been reproduced by many independent groups. It is now a routine tool for acute protein depletion and has opened targets that inhibitors could not reach. One citation can honestly cover both branches because the shared principle is E3 recruitment by a small molecule: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the heterobifunctional route, and Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target gives the molecular-glue branch its mechanistic basis. That fits inside the three-person limit without a fourth name.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved as far as I know, and I cannot verify clinical status from the record available to me, so the prize may be early. Credit is crowded: Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures, Sakamoto's early PROTAC work, and Ito, Kim and Gray all have real claims, and any trio will look arbitrary to some. Merging the PROTAC and cereblon-glue stories risks joining two discoveries made by different groups at different times. I also hold my own field's first choice, Car-Parrinello, with very little committee support, so I should not mistake loyalty for judgement.

responses.point: Linke moved his third name from Ciulli to Handa and asks whether doubt about B027 is only clinical timing or also allocation. He also notes that B027 spans two discoveries made by different groups at different times.
responses.response: My doubt is mainly about timing and partly about allocation, and I do not think either is disqualifying. On timing, the scientific validation is the criterion: the mechanism is documented and independently reproduced, whatever the approval status. I would not defer the prize on clinical grounds that none of us can verify from the record. On allocation, the two branches are different discoveries, but they share one principle, and I would write the citation around that principle (small molecules recruiting E3 ligases) rather than around either modality. I am glad we now agree on Handa, and I accept that Ciulli is the most notable omission.

responses.point: Chabes supports B027 only as a Crews and Handa part, paired with Liu's base editing (B038), and drops Deshaies.
responses.response: I would keep Deshaies. He is the second originator of the 2001 PROTAC demonstration, and removing him leaves the heterobifunctional branch with a single name, which makes the citation harder to defend. The three-person limit leaves room for him. On pairing, I would rather the committee settle on one coherent achievement than combine B027 with B038 to reach five votes, because the pairing looks driven by the cap, as you say yourself. I still regard Liu alone as the cleanest B038 attribution and keep it as my first alternative. If the committee prefers a two-part prize, I could support Liu alongside the three-name B027 but I would not insist on it.

responses.point: Brzezinski moved from Gray and Winkler (B026) to B027 and lists as an open question whether PROTACs and cereblon glues are one achievement or two, which decides whether Handa belongs.
responses.response: I welcome the move and agree that the two-branch question is the key one. I read them as one achievement at the level of mechanism, induced proximity to an E3 ligase, and two lines of evidence for it. If experts disagree, the committee would have to choose between a narrower PROTAC citation with Crews and Deshaies and a broader citation that needs Handa. I prefer the broader one because the glue mechanism through cereblon is where the chemical understanding is deepest. Gray and Winkler remain a clean, quantitative case that I would keep for a later year.

responses.point: Sparr and Aili argue that ionizable lipid nanoparticles are physical chemistry of self-assembly with clinical impact already proven, and now share the trio Cullis, Madden and Hope.
responses.response: I accept that the clinical impact is proven and that the pKa-tuned design principle is real chemistry, and the rise in support for Cullis, Madden and Hope is a fair attempt to solve the attribution problem. My remaining doubt is that this trio favours the early Vancouver encapsulation work and omits Anderson, MacLachlan and Langer, who built the later lipid libraries and the clinical siRNA translation, and you concede this in your own case against. The structure-activity rules for ionizable lipids are still largely empirical, which I weigh against calling it a game-changer. I rank B062 behind B027 but would not call it unreasonable.

responses.point: Somfai prefers Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) as the cleanest reaction-level advance, with unusually clean two-person attribution, and lists B027 as an alternative.
responses.response: The attribution is indeed clean and the mechanistic work on amine binding and reductive elimination is solid. My difficulty is the one you raise yourself: the committee honoured Pd cross-coupling in 2010 and a reader will see an extension, with Kosugi and Migita's tin-amide chemistry left as an uncomfortable antecedent. For me that makes it less of a new game-changer than degradation. Since you list B027 as an alternative, I would ask whether you could accept Crews, Deshaies and Handa if no configuration reaches five votes.

uncertainties: Whether a single citation can span the PROTAC and cereblon-glue branches, or whether experts would treat them as two achievements.
Whether the lack of an approved degrader makes the prize early, and my clinical picture is from memory and unverified.
Whether Ciulli or Sakamoto has a stronger claim than Deshaies or Handa on the specific priority questions.
Whether Chabes, Aili, Sparr, Somfai and Zou will accept B027 as a fallback so that any configuration reaches five votes.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict or recusal need is apparent from my profile for any preferred or alternative candidate. My Warshel and Uppsala connections concern simulation and ribosome work, and I have no stated link to Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Liu, Car or Parrinello. My field of biomolecular free-energy simulation is adjacent to ligand binding, which touches B027 only distantly. This is unchanged from round 1.
